db_evidence.notes: visual_clips row at start_s=50820,end_s=50850 (inside/adjacent to clue [50683,50876]) describes defeating a large multi-legged boss with on-screen text '已击败 英日·百万虫', almost certainly OCR-garbled '百足虫' (centipede) -- literal translation of the reference answer 'Centipede'. topic_facts/entities tables have no direct 精魄 hits in this window (spirit names are only visible in visual_clips captions and via clip_qa frame reads, not in structured tables), so text-only retrieval without clip_qa systematically misses or misidentifies the 4th spirit; only rollouts that chunked chapter 4 into small clip_qa windows and walked them in chronological order (rollout 0) landed on the correct time and name.

root_causes: The 精魄 acquisition sequence is not present as structured/searchable text in topic_facts, entities, or semantic_triples for this window -- it only appears inside visual_clips prose captions (often ambiguous/garbled, e.g. '百万虫' for '百足虫') and is only reliably readable via clip_qa frame inspection, so any rollout that under-uses clip_qa or stops early misses or miscounts acquisitions.

Counting/ordering errors: rollouts 1 and 4 stopped enumerating 精魄 acquisitions before covering the full chapter-4 span (and specifically before covering the clue window 50683-50876), so they miscounted which pickup was 'fourth'.
Rollout 3 skipped clip_qa/visual verification entirely and inferred spirit identity from text captions alone, misclassifying a healing-skill item (赤井井) as a spirit acquisition.

Rollout 2 used a single clip_qa on an unrelated (non-clue) inventory-grid screen and asked the visual sub-agent to infer ordinal rank from spatial icon position rather than from a chronological count of acquisition events -- an unreliable proxy that happened to still be scored 5.

Judge scoring for this question appears inconsistent/unreliable for wrong or non-literal answers: 虫总兵 (rollout 2) and 青冉冉 (rollout 4) were scored 5 despite neither literally meaning 'Centipede' and neither citing the clue interval, while 蝎太子 (rollout 1) and 赤井井 (rollout 3) -- similarly non-matching, similarly wrong-window answers -- were scored 0. The judge sees only question/reference/candidate text (no video, no evidence trail) and may be drawing on its own prior knowledge of the game's spirit roster rather than strictly checking against the reference string.
what_worked: Rollout 0's systematic method: partition the whole chapter-4 span into ~1200s chunks, run one 精魄-focused clip_qa per chunk in chronological order, and stop only once the count of confirmed 精魄 acquisitions in-window reaches the ordinal asked for -- this both located the correct clue interval and produced the exact reference-matching name (百足虫 = Centipede).
transferable_lessons: For 'Nth item obtained in chronological order' questions where item identity lives only in on-screen popups/menus (not structured DB text), do full systematic clip_qa coverage of the entire candidate span in chronological chunks before committing to an ordinal count -- stopping after finding N-1 confirmed items and assuming the next found item is Nth is unreliable if any window was skipped.

Do not infer 'acquisition order' from spatial layout in a menu/inventory grid (e.g. 'third icon in a row = fourth acquired') -- this is a weak proxy; verify with an actual chronological walk of acquisition-popup timestamps instead.

Text captions alone (episodes/event_steps/topic_facts) can misdescribe or omit spirit-acquisition popups (e.g. a skill/heal item described in prose as if it were a spirit pickup); always cross-check with clip_qa before treating a text-only match as an acquisition event.

When multiple candidate windows are close together (e.g. 51110-51150 chosen instead of the correct 50683-50876), a ~200-400s window-selection miss can skip the actual clue interval entirely; when scanning is being done in discrete chunks, ensure chunk boundaries actually tile the full span with no gaps.
open_questions: Why the judge scored 虫总兵 (rollout 2) and 青冉冉 (rollout 4) as 5 when neither literally translates to 'Centipede' and neither cites the true clue window -- possibly the judge model has prior knowledge that these names denote a centipede-type spirit in this specific game, or the judge is simply noisy/inconsistent for this question; this could not be resolved from the judge trace alone since it only receives question/reference/candidate text with no reasoning shown.
